questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning of Production' refers to.
questions.a: Production is the process of combining various material inputs and immaterial inputs to make goods and services that satisfy human wants and needs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning of Production'.
questions.a: Production converts inputs (factors of production) into outputs (goods and services) that have value and utility for consumers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meaning of Production' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Introduction to Production

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Factors of Production' refers to.
questions.a: Factors of production are the resources or inputs used in the production of goods and services. The four main factors are land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Factors of Production'.
questions.a: No single factor alone can produce anything; all four factors -- land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship -- must be combined in appropriate proportions for production to take place.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Factors of Production' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Factors of Production

concepts.title: Land as a Factor of Production

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Land as a Factor of Production' refers to.
questions.a: Land, as a factor of production, refers to all natural resources used in production. It includes not only the surface of the earth but also forests, water, minerals, and other gifts of nature.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Land as a Factor of Production'.
questions.a: Land is a passive factor of production. It is fixed in supply, has no cost of production, and is heterogeneous in quality, but it provides the base and raw materials for all production.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Land as a Factor of Production'.
questions.a: Define land as a factor of production.

concepts.title: Labour as a Factor of Production

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Labour as a Factor of Production' refers to.
questions.a: Labour is the human physical and mental effort used in the production of goods and services. It is one of the four factors of production.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Labour as a Factor of Production'.
questions.a: Labour is an active factor of production. It cannot be separated from the worker, it is perishable, it has a weak bargaining power, and its supply generally increases with wages up to a point.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Labour as a Factor of Production'.
questions.a: Define labour as a factor of production.

concepts.title: Capital as a Factor of Production

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Capital as a Factor of Production' refers to.
questions.a: Capital refers to all man-made goods that are used in the production of other goods and services. It includes machinery, tools, buildings, raw materials, and money invested in production.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Capital as a Factor of Production'.
questions.a: Capital is a produced means of production. It is man-made, can be classified as physical capital (machines, tools) and human capital (skills, education), and it enhances the productivity of land and labour.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Capital as a Factor of Production'.
questions.a: Define capital as a factor of production.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Physical and Human Capital' refers to.
questions.a: Physical capital consists of tangible, man-made assets such as machines, tools, buildings, and raw materials used in production. Human capital consists of the knowledge, skills, training, and health of workers that enhance their productivity.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Physical and Human Capital'.
questions.a: Physical capital improves production by providing better tools and equipment, while human capital improves production by making workers more skilled and efficient. Both are essential for modern production.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Physical and Human Capital'.
questions.a: Define physical capital with two examples.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Entrepreneurship and Organisation' refers to.
questions.a: Entrepreneurship is the factor of production that involves organising the other factors -- land, labour, and capital -- and taking the risk of running a business to produce goods or services.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Entrepreneurship and Organisation'.
questions.a: The entrepreneur brings together land, labour, and capital, makes decisions about what and how to produce, and bears the risk of profit or loss. Without entrepreneurship, the other factors remain unorganised and unproductive.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Entrepreneurship and Organisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Entrepreneurship

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Role of Technology in Production' refers to.
questions.a: Technology refers to the methods, processes, and equipment used to convert inputs into outputs. In production, technology determines how efficiently land, labour, and capital are combined to produce goods and services.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Role of Technology in Production'.
questions.a: Better technology allows more output to be produced with the same inputs, or the same output with fewer inputs. It improves quality, reduces cost, and enables new kinds of products.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Role of Technology in Production' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Technology and Production

questions.q: Using the method 'Productivity and Efficiency', work with: input = 3, output = 12. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of productivity.
questions.a: 4 units

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Productivity and Efficiency' and work with: input = 3, output = 40. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of productivity.
questions.a: 13.3333 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Productivity and Efficiency' refers to.
questions.a: Productivity is the ratio of output produced to the inputs used. Efficiency refers to how well inputs are utilised to produce output without waste. Higher productivity and efficiency mean more output is obtained from the same or fewer inputs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Productivity and Efficiency'.
questions.a: Productivity measures how much output is produced per unit of input. Efficiency measures how well resources are used without waste. Improving technology, skills, and organisation can raise both productivity and efficiency.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Productivity and Efficiency', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: Productivity = Output / Input
